records.reason: A mundane primal spellcasting focus/adornment; the whole text is flavour and permission to hold it, no number or capability.
Downtime production machine (pages per day, type-setting hours); nothing touches the owner's sheet.

Relic Air gift: the relic casts fly ON YOU once per hour, and nothing gives the owner that spell. The once-per-hour pips already come from item.frequency (itemUses.ts), but the spell itself is absent. Same lane as living-storm / living-statue, which do ship innateSpells.
Explicitly provides the full normal range of function and no bonus; pure flavour/accessibility.
An activation that damages ENEMIES in a burst and resolves at once; nothing standing on the owner.
Injury poison applied to a TARGET (save DC, stages); the GM runs the affliction on the victim.
Catalyst: the added persistent bleed hits creatures ADJACENT to you who fail a Reflex save, i.e. targets, resolved when the shield spell's Shield Block fires.
Mundane object whose entire content is a DC 25 skill check the GM adjudicates; no owner-side change.
As the base puzzle box plus a negligible-Bulk hidden compartment; a GM-adjudicated DC and a container detail.
Mundane object; only a DC 20 skill check the GM adjudicates.
DC 20 puzzle plus a 1-inch hidden compartment; nothing mechanical on the owner.
Umbrella/hollow entry listing the whole puzzle-box family's DCs; a GM-adjudicated check and a tiny compartment.
Mundane object; only a DC 15 skill check the GM adjudicates.
DC 15 puzzle plus a 1-inch hidden compartment; nothing mechanical on the owner.

Activation summons a SEPARATE creature (a Giant Rat with its own 2 actions) run at the table/in the tracker; no standing change to the owner, and the once-per-day pip is already synthesized from item.frequency by itemUses.ts, exactly like the other wondrous figurines.

Registered as an etchable armor property rune in core.runes ('quenching', slot armor, kind property) and etchable via planRune in src/rules/attachments.ts; its only effect is the DC of a persistent-damage flat check rolled at the table.
In core.runes as an armor property rune (level 10); etchable via planRune. Its effect is a persistent-damage flat-check DC rolled at the table.

The text explicitly says you receive NO special benefits from either outfit; it is appearance only plus 3 Interact actions.
In core.runes as a weapon property rune ('quickstrike', level 16) and etchable via planRune; the quickened it confers is tracked on the sheet's conditions tracker, which already carries quickened.
A purchasable pet whose own note says it cannot be combat trained or contribute to combat in any way.
A purchasable pet whose own note says it cannot be combat trained or contribute to combat in any way.
An activation resolved in the moment: three Strides and damage to the object/creature you ram (a TARGET, basic Reflex); nothing standing on the owner, and the per-hour pip comes from item.frequency.
In core.runes as an armor property rune ('raiment', level 5), etchable via planRune; its whole effect is cosmetic — the text says the armor's statistics don't change.

Relic Earth gift: the owner casts 5th-rank wall of stone once per day and nothing gives them the spell. The daily pip already comes from item.frequency, but the casting itself is absent — the same lane living-statue / living-storm already use.

A class kit is bought precisely so the listed gear lands in the inventory, but buying it adds one inert line item — the leather armor, dagger and adventurer's-pack contents never appear. The app already has the expansion mechanism (KIT_CONTENTS in src/rules/play.ts, used by addInventoryItem); only 'adventurers-pack' is registered in it. NOTE: this is that code table, not an Item field.

fix.where: KIT_CONTENTS in src/rules/play.ts (the adventurer's-pack expansion table) — there is no item-level field for kit contents

records.reason: Activated ammunition that tells you how far it flew; pure information, no check modifier and no lasting change.
A mundane tool: it doubles exploration-mode descent rate off your Climb result, which is not a modifier to any check or Speed value; the GM resolves the distance.
A purchasable pet whose own note says it cannot be combat trained or contribute to combat in any way.
Ammunition whose whole effect (deafened, stupefied 1, loss of lifesense) lands on the TARGET it damages.
Ammunition whose whole effect lands on the TARGET it damages; only the DC scales.
Accessibility item: it reads aloud languages the wearer is ALREADY fluent in, at normal reading speed, with no limit — it adds no language, no check bonus and no resource.

It grants reading comprehension of any script, not spoken fluency, and it explicitly is not invested. The only legal lane (passiveEffects.grantsLanguages) is invested-only (build.ts:3264) and lists concrete language ids, so using it would over-grant full spoken languages — worse than the gap. Left to the table.

In core.runes as an armor property rune ('ready', level 6) and etchable via planRune; its only effect is how many actions donning armor takes, which is downtime/exploration action economy with no sheet number.
In core.runes as an armor property rune (level 11), etchable via planRune; effect is donning action economy only.

Its +1 striking is a fundamental-rune matter, and fundamental runes are modelled (WeaponRunes on the inventory instance, set in the item editor / by etching, consumed by the strike math in derive.ts). The rest — a 3-dose poison reservoir and a reaction that poisons the creature you hit — is poison applied to a TARGET.

A specific +1 wounding striking scythe: the fundamentals are modelled by the rune system, and 'wounding' exists in core.runes as an etchable weapon property rune; the weapon's own d10 slashing / deadly-d10 / trip statistics are read directly by the strike code.

The thread has exactly six knots and each Untie Fate consumes one permanently, after which it becomes non-magical — a finite pool the player must track, and the item carries no counter (it has no 'frequency' either, so itemUses.ts synthesizes nothing). The reaction's effect (downgrading your own critical failure) is resolved at the table, but the six charges are the owner's resource.
Ammunition; the shrinking, reach loss and enfeebled all land on the TARGET that fails its save.
The item entry is just the physical object (its text is empty); the Regalia implement's mechanics live in core.implement.regalia and the thaumaturge class features that read it.

The surcoat's Speed penalty is an unconditional standing change to the owner ('increases the Speed penalty of your armor by 5 feet') and nothing delivers it — the item carries no fields at all. Only the penalty is expressible: the physical resistance is conditional (critical hits only) and item resistances have no 'when', so modelling it would over-grant flat resistance.

An activation that detonates attuned bombs; the splash damage lands on creatures in the bombs' squares (TARGETS) and the attunement is table bookkeeping over separate bomb items.
A mundane tool whose whole content is permission to Repair with Crafting (downtime), plus a free draw/replace.
Saves one Interact action when swapping a magazine — pure action economy at the table; reload counts live on the weapon and there is no field for an action-cost reduction.
An ammunition container; the reload cost and volley are the weapon's statistics, which the strike code reads directly.

A spare part for a Water Purifier; the +5 counteract modifier is the purifier's roll against a disease/poison in the water, made by the device at the table, not a modifier on any of the owner's statistics.
